correctness.rationale: For every \(0<h<1\), antipodal averaging gives \(F_h=\pi^2/4+\langle\arcsin^2(\langle x,v\rangle)\rangle\). The absolutely convergent arcsine-square series yields \(G(r)=\operatorname{Li}_2(r^2)/2\). Periodic integration by parts gives normal equatorial Taylor coefficient \(1+\log h\); direct Taylor expansion gives polar coefficient \([1-h\arcsin(h)/\sqrt{1-h^2}]/2\). Monotonicity yields a unique polar threshold, and differentiating the two exact energies proves their unique crossing strictly between \(2/5\) and \(7/10\), inside the coexistence interval. The proof explicitly excludes zero-Hessian boundaries and global classification. The standalone standard-library verifier executed and passed 48 diagnostic comparisons; finite tests are supplemental, not a substitute for proof.

value.rationale: Intrinsic Fréchet energies on positively curved spaces need not be geodesically convex. The natural symmetric two-latitude model exhibits a mathematically structural coexistence of isolated and continuous locally minimizing components over the exact open interval \((e^{-1},h_{\rm ax})\). Unlike mere local Taylor evaluation, the result identifies both exact sharp Hessian thresholds, a dilogarithmic energy integral and a unique inner crossover where competing stable orbit energies exchange order. It supplies an explicit benchmark for multimodal spherical mean geometry and optimization; global minimizers and critical-boundary quartics are not asserted.
